page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u2i-c1m2.4xlarge is an x86_64 virtual machine instance powered by a KVM hypervisor. The instance features 16 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon processor operating at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz. System memory is configured at 32.0 GB, establishing a compute-focused ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated hardware accelerators, featuring zero GPUs.

Network connectivity is provisioned with a baseline bandwidth of 10 Gbps, supporting stable throughput for distributed traffic and inter-service communication. The instance does not bundle local disk storage, necessitating the attachment of external network block storage for operating system images and persistent application data. Complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not included.

With its 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation, ecs.u2i-c1m2.4xlarge offers resource density that prioritizes CPU-intensive tasks over memory capacity. This makes the configuration cost-efficient for workloads requiring high thread concurrency without the overhead of excess memory allocation. Typical applications include batch processing, distributed build environments, CI/CD runners, and application serving layers.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u2i-c1m2.4xlarge is an x86_64 server instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It is configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.7 GHz, paired with 32.0 GB of memory. This yields a 1:2 compute-dense ratio of 2.0 GB RAM per core. The instance provides 10 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth and contains no dedicated GPU hardware or local NVMe storage, relying entirely on network-attached block devices for persistence. Complimentary public IPv4 addresses are omitted. By optimizing CPU density against a moderate memory footprint, the server delivers efficient resource utilization for multi-threaded processing where massive memory caches are unnecessary. It is appropriately provisioned for batch compute, continuous integration pipelines, microservices hosting, and medium-scale web server fleets.
